posts.name: Divyanshu
posts.cooked:
While following the instructions in the course video for generating an SSH key, I encountered a problem. When I run the ssh-keygen command on my Windows system, it generates an ED25519 key pair by default. However, as shown in the course video and per the course requirements, an RSA key is expected.

Here is the command and output I am getting:

C:\Users\ASUS TUF>ssh-keygen
Generating public/private ed25519 key pair.
Enter file in which to save the key (C:\Users\ASUS TUF/.ssh/id_ed25519):
…

Could you please guide me on how to explicitly generate an RSA key instead of ED25519?

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
DivyanshuMishra:

it generates an ED25519 key pair by default

You can submit ED25519 key. ED25519 is a modern public-key signature system based on elliptic curve cryptography (ECC). Both of them work fine.

posts.name: Hemant Nishad
posts.cooked:
ED25519 key works, if you intentionally want to use rsa key, use following command:
“ssh-keygen -t rsa”

posts.name: Divyanshu
posts.cooked:
Alemniscate:

ssh-keygen -t rsa

yes i did as you say and i could generate my ssh key and when i pasted it at https://vm-manager-se2001-781744309994.asia-south1.run.app/passwordless witout any error but now to connect with remote machine when i wrote the command

ssh 23f100__70@se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in

i got error

C:\Users\ASUS TUF>ssh 23f1002270@se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in
ssh: connect to host se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in port 22: Connection timed out

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: @DivyanshuMishra this looks like a client side connectivity issue. Can you try with a different network such as mobile data?

posts.name: Hemant Nishad
posts.cooked:
check if your internet is fast enough, maybe try changing your network.
This happens with me when i try to connect using my institutes wifi network. I prefer my phone hotspot for VM.
